correctness.rationale: For k≥1, write rho^k(0)=AB with A=rho^(k−1)(0), B=rho^(k−1)(1). A cyclic window of length at most 2|A| is contained in ABA or BAB according to its starting block; these equal rho^(k−1)(010) or rho^(k−1)(101). Both base trigrams occur in the substitution fixed point, so every cyclic factor occurs linearly in the infinite word. The 8 admissible preimage digrams form a substitution-closed set, and all occur by rho^4(0). Four exact length-16 coded supertiles span all windows up to length 16, giving 36 palindromes and none at lengths 15/16. Centered factors preclude any palindrome ≥15. Exhaustive circular enumeration of k=0..8 and explicit occurrence of all 36 linear palindromes inside R_8 prove sharp stabilization at k=8; nested dyadic prefixes preserve inclusion. Independent checker corroborates the finite exact ingredients; the general containment comes from the three-block embedding.

value.rationale: Cyclic closing can create new factors absent from the infinite sequence; proving it never happens at any scale for this distinguished automatic word is a structural boundary-fidelity theorem, with a sharp exact stabilization of all cyclic palindromes. The ordinary 36-word count is prior-derived support only; the independently useful cyclic theorem and rank are mathematically substantive.

limitations: The ordinary palindrome language enumeration is not itself novel; it is a corollary of known maximal ordinary palindromes.
The cyclic-factor proof has a length bound ≤2^k and does not extend to arbitrary prefixes or occurrence multiplicities.
